queries.details:
The eligibility or class description details in the document.

Extract Eligibility and route them based on specificity. If values are provided separately for Class 1, Class 2, and/or Class 3 services, populate only the corresponding class-level fields and leave the general Eligibility field blank. Do not duplicate values into the general row.
If only a  Eligibility value is stated without class distinctions, populate only the general Eligibility field and leave all Class 1, Class 2, and Class 3 fields blank.

Extract any explicit employee-group descriptor that applies generally to all eligible employees
and is NOT tied to a specific class number.

This field captures broad eligibility groupings only when classes are not defined.

Examples include:
- Employees working 30 hours or more per week
- All Eligible Employees
- All Non-US Employees

Populate this field ONLY if no explicit Class 1 / Class 2 / Class 3 group labels exist.

Do NOT:
- infer class structure
- normalize wording
- extract hours, waiting periods, or effective dates

entities.criteria: Text describing which employees are eligible for LTD coverage and how eligible employees are grouped into classes, including employment status, hours worked, waiting period, and class definitions.

Description of employee group classified as Class 1 for eligibility purposes. 

Extract the explicit employee-group label assigned to Class 1.

If the document distinguishes employee groups by pay type (Hourly vs Salaried):

 output: Hourly Employees for Class 1.
If the document labels Hourly as Class 2, reassign it to Class 1 in output.
If pay type is not used, extract the explicit Class 1 label exactly as written.

Rules:
Capture only the group identity.
Normalize pay-type classes so Hourly = Class 1.
Do not include eligibility mechanics.

Other valid Class 1 group labels include:
- Executives and VPs
- Full Time Employees
- All Non-US Employees

Description of employee group classified as Class 2 for eligibility purposes.

Extract the explicit employee-group label assigned to Class 2.

If the document distinguishes employee groups by pay type (Hourly vs Salaried):
 output: Salaried Employees for Class 2.

If the document labels Salaried as Class 1, reassign it to Class 2 in output.

If pay type is not used, extract the explicit Class 2 label exactly as written.

Rules:
Capture only the group identity.
Normalize pay-type classes so Salaried = Class 2.
Do not include eligibility mechanics.

Other valid Class 2 group labels include:
- Full Time Employees
- Part Time Employees
- All US Employees

Description of employee group classified as Class 3 for eligibility purposes.

Extract the explicit employee-group label assigned to Class 3, if present.

Valid labels include job category, employment type, or geography.

Apply the same rules as Class 1 / Class 2.

Extract the elimination period required before benefits are payable.
Return the duration verbatim as stated, limited to numeric value and unit only (e.g., “180 days”).

Output format:
<number> days

Rules:
- Use lowercase "days"
- No leading/trailing spaces
- No extra text

queries.details:
Locate the Maximum Benefit Duration by finding the section or table that defines how long LTD benefits are payable (e.g., “Maximum Benefit Duration,” “Duration of Benefits,” or age-based schedules).

If the document presents Maximum Benefit Duration in a class-based table (e.g., Class 1, Class 2, Class 3), extract the duration exactly as stated for each class. Do not infer or combine class values.

When Maximum Benefit Duration differs by class, leave the global Maximum Benefit Duration blank and populate only the applicable class-level values.


Return only the duration phrase (e.g., “5 Years”, “SSNRA”, “To SSNRA”, “Age 65”, etc.).

Do not infer, standardize, combine, or modify the wording.
If multiple classes exist, extract the duration for each class exactly as shown.
Do not pull duration language from Life Waiver of Premium sections.

Extract the disability definition wherever it appears in the document. If definitions match across documents, the summary must reflect identical results and must not return null.

Definition and conditions under which partial disability benefits apply. 
Identify the Partial Disability benefit type based on how benefits are calculated.

If benefits are based on percentage of earnings lost, classify as
"Proportionate (Residual) Loss"

If benefits increase by stages or over time independent of earnings loss, classify as
"Progressive Partial Disability"

Do not infer “progressive” unless explicitly stated.

Criteria used to determine ongoing disability based on post-disability earnings or work capacity.

Normalize the gainful earnings threshold into the format:
Own Occupation % / Any Occupation %.

If only one percentage is stated and no distinction between own and any occupation is made, apply the same percentage to both (e.g., 80% → 80% / 80%).

If separate percentages are stated for own and any occupation periods, reflect both values accordingly (e.g., 80% own and 60% any → 80% / 60%).

Standardize formatting as percentages with a space-separated slash (e.g., “80% / 80%”).

Extract any explicit limitation on benefit duration that applies to disabilities
described as self-reported or subjective in nature, including language such as
"self-reported symptoms," "subjective symptoms," or conditions defined as
primarily based on the insured’s report of pain, fatigue, or similar symptoms.

Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).

Do not infer self-reported limitations from mental illness, substance abuse,
or condition lists unless the policy explicitly ties the limitation to
self-reported or subjective symptoms.
Limitations on benefit duration for disabilities caused by mental or nervous conditions. Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).
Limitations on benefit duration for disabilities related to substance or alcohol abuse. Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).
Benefit provision encouraging return to work while receiving LTD benefits. Return duration only (e.g., 24 months).

queries.details:
Premium details exactly as it is written on the document. Premium Calculation Rules:
Monthly and Annual Premium fields are calculated outputs and must never be populated directly from carrier documents.
Any premium values found in documents are reference-only and must not be extracted. Monthly and Annual Premiums must always be whole-dollar amounts.

entities.criteria:
Extract the covered payroll or benefit volume used for pricing (the exposure base). This value represents volume, not cost.
Do not extract rates, premiums, or percentages for this field.
Only populate this field when the document explicitly identifies covered payroll, benefit volume, or exposure used for pricing.
Source this value from the Renewal document and apply the same value across all carriers (Current, Renewal, and Alternative).

Total monthly LTD premium. Do not extract from the document.
Calculate as:
Rate × (Estimated Monthly Volume ÷ rate basis unit)
Example: If rate basis is per $100 of payroll, divide volume by 100 before applying the rate.

After calculating the Monthly Premium using the approved formula, round the result to the nearest whole dollar.
Do not retain cents.

Total annual LTD premium. Do not extract from the document.
Calculate as:
Monthly Premium × 12.

Do not copy carrier-stated annual premiums. Do not independently round the Annual Premium and do not derive it directly from volume.

Percentage increase or decrease from prior LTD rates. 
If a percentage change is explicitly stated, return that value.

Otherwise calculate as:
(Renewal Rate − Current Rate) ÷ Current Rate × 100
The Client Name as stated in the LTD plan,

Extract the plan effective date or coverage period exactly as stated in the document. Look for effective dates on the front cover, first page, Summary of Benefits (SOB), benefit plan year section, or within “amended and restated as of” language. Capture the date text as written and do not substitute eligibility language.
